notes.body:
The concept of the condensation of heat (تَكَاثُفُ الْحَرَارَةِ) is a profound spiritual metaphor describing the miraculous origin of our physical world. From primordial darkness—a creative source, not an empty void—Allah brings forth an intense, formless energy, termed the **condensation of heat**.

Like invisible steam gathering and cooling into solid water droplets, this process describes how powerful, non-physical energy becomes dense, tangible, and structured. This transformation of the intangible forms the material realm, giving rise to the **seven earths and all their sustenances**.

This creation establishes a cosmic balance. Just as smoke, born from water, rises to form the seven heavens, this condensed heat, born from darkness, settles to form the seven earths. This pairing—heaven light and ethereal, earth dense and material—reflects a fundamental duality throughout creation.
etymology: تَكَاثُف (condensation): From the root ك-ث-ف, which means to be thick, dense, or numerous. The form تَفَاعُل implies a process of becoming something. Thus, تَكَاثُف is the process of becoming dense, perfectly describing how a diffuse energy gathers to form a solid, material reality like the earth.

حَرَارَة (heat): From the root ح-ر-ر, which means to be hot. This root also carries the meaning of being free or liberated. This connection suggests that the primordial heat was a free, unbound energy, and its condensation represents this energy becoming bound and structured into the forms of the physical world.
